newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Ocean Group to march to 600p.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Ocean Group to march to 600p.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-50 * MA-200
+ Breakout from a month long consolidation by shares of Ocean Group implies the stock can now advance to 600p over the long-term, technical analysts said.

+ The stock's medium and long-term moving averages are following the share price higher -- indicating a bull trend -- and this was confirmed by above average turnover on breakout and a revival in its relative strength against the All-Share index.
Shares of freight management company Ocean Group look set to march higher continuing an uptrend begun in February, technical analysts said.

"The shares are breaking out of a line consolidation in which they have been for a month between support at 520p and resistance at 530p," said Richard Marshall, a director at Investment Research of Cambridge Ltd.
"The shares look capable of another advance to a target at 600p (long-term)," he added.
By 0900 GMT, Ocean Group shares were unchanged at 539-1/2p. The shares are in the Mid-250 index.

Ocean Group shares began to climb from a low of 446p in mid-February before flattening out a few weeks later at around 530p. This flattening period between March to May has allowed the stock's various moving averages to converge towards the share price before romping ahead once more.
"Recent support from a sharply rising 50-day moving average suggests the medium-term uptrend is still very much intact," said Marshall.
Turnover in the shares has also increased as they broke away from their consolidation phase over the past few days implying upward pressure for the shares, analysts said.
Daily average volume over the past five days has been about 490,000 shares traded as the stock broke higher compared with 140,000 over the previous five days.

The flatness of the share price has meant Ocean Group has been underperforming the market -- as measured by the All-Share index -- for several weeks but its recent flight to higher levels has arrested that underperformance and a chart of the stock's relative strength against the index may also be close to making an upward break.
"The longer-term trend on both the share price and the relative strength ratio is bullish," said Marshall.
